pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind cleanup

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
This PR adds a test to test the following untested endpoints:

* replaceCoreV1NamespacedPodStatus
* readCoreV1NamespacedPodStatus
* listCoreV1PodForAllNamespaces
* deleteCoreV1CollectionNamespacedPod

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #90936

**Special notes for your reviewer**:
Adds +4 endpoint test coverage (good for conformance)

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```
NONE
```

**Release note:**
```release-note
NONE
```

**Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.**:

```
NONE
```

/sig testing
/sig architecture
/area conformance

At this point, given we know there are latent flakes, I would recommend focusing on root causing and resolving those rather than trying to trigger more failures. Digging into the logs for the existing failures would be where I would start. (several failures linked from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/93405)

I would also recommend moving this to 1.20

The only things going into 1.19 now are release blockers, cleanup things like OWNER file fixup, and things improving CI signal by reducing flakes

[PR History](https://prow.k8s.io/pr-history/?org=kubernetes&repo=kubernetes&pr=93459) shows a single clean run. Checking again for any flakes

review_comments: Isn't there the possibility that the kubelet has already updated the pod's ready condition back to true here?

I might be wrong, but from my understand the response from the API server (in this case `podStatusUpdate`) is basically the same as the request. If that 's true then it should be fine to do this, otherwise I'll remove the checks after the update (so the endpoint is hit)
Ah, I misread the code, and thought we were doing a separate retrieval
